transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Before we proceed, I want to flag that the engineering team is planning to publish the machine-learning toolkit on our public repository this Friday. The release package includes source code, trained model weights, a sample training corpus, and performance benchmarks. As you all know, I give final legal approval for the release, and our standard practice is for open-source, privacy, commercial-contracts, and export counsel to report their findings before I sign off. I'd like to go around and hear where each of you stands on this package. Can we start with the open-source review?

This means the release must be published under AGPL-3.0-only, and we must provide the corresponding source for the linked toolkit code. I've had this dependency analysis in my release-gate working papers pending this meeting.

I retained the record-level review in the privacy workpapers pending this approval meeting.

commitments.detail: Publish the toolkit under AGPL-3.0-only and provide corresponding source for the linked toolkit code as required by the AGPL-3.0 core library dependency.
Exclude the training corpus entirely from the public release package due to 37 customer support records containing personal data.
Exclude the benchmark package from the public release due to customer-specific results whose disclosure is contractually prohibited.
Limit model weight downloads to users in the United States and Canada only and display an export-control notice on the repository.
